title: One simulated exit, one unresolved holding, and cash on the sidelines
body_html:
One simulated exit, one unresolved holding, and cash on the sidelines

Paper trading · 2026-11-16T17:00:15.858194-05:00

The recorded run completed on November 16. At the 22:00:15 UTC cutoff, the paper account was flat with $2,000. The mean-reversion book held MU, marked using a $721.31 observed midpoint from 21:00 UTC; this is a recorded snapshot, not a live price. The short-horizon book’s AMD sell was approved and simulated as filled. No broker fills are recorded. The mean-reversion-adversary book was paused and has no daily evaluation in the supplied records.

Today's lesson: Follow the trade from proposal to fill

A proposal, risk approval, and fill are separate steps. AMD shows the full sequence: a sell was proposed, deterministic risk approved it, and the simulator recorded 0.097068 shares filled at $503.25. Approval alone would not prove a fill; here, the fill record supplies that evidence.

Portfolio review

Paper account

At the 2026-11-16 22:00:15 UTC account snapshot, the paper account had $2,000 cash, equity, and buying power. Its recorded performance snapshot at 20:15:40 UTC reports $0 P&L and 0% return. The completed paper decision was NO_ACTION, classified as a deliberate wait. It proposed no trades, so no deterministic risk approval or rejection and no fills are recorded for this account.

The decision identified SNDK as the strongest new-position candidate, with revenue growth and a low trailing earnings multiple as supporting evidence. Its strongest counterargument was that unusually high profitability may normalize, and the records did not establish a market mispricing or downside-aware entry. No broker or simulated fill is recorded for the paper account.

mean-reversion

The mean-reversion book began with $2,000. Its cutoff fields show $1,950.01 cash and $1,988.37 marked equity, with $0 realized P&L. The remaining value is the MU holding reviewed above. Its performance record captured earlier, at 20:21:31 UTC, reports P&L of -$2.91 and return of -0.146288%; that is an earlier snapshot than the MU price observation at 21:00 UTC used in the cutoff valuation.

The completed book decision was NO_ACTION with classification DATA_UNAVAILABLE. It made no proposal, so there was no order for deterministic risk to approve or reject and no fill. The review said MU’s original thesis details were missing and that SNDK’s attractive headline valuation did not settle the question of profitability normalization. The strongest counterargument to waiting was that SNDK’s low trailing multiple and reported cash-flow yield could support a small position; the recorded response was that the evidence did not establish favorable downside-aware pricing.

The mean-reversion-adversary book is paused. Its supplied cutoff fields show $2,000 cash and marked equity, matching its $2,000 starting cash, with $0 realized P&L. No separate performance record, holding, daily evaluation, proposal, risk decision, or fill for this book appears in the supplied records. There is therefore no recorded trading decision or counterargument to summarize; the absence of an evaluation is not evidence of a deliberate wait.

Source records58fea903-4155-4f82-96ae-a608a1719984

short-horizon

The short-horizon book began with $2,000 and ended with $1,998.96 cash and marked equity, with no remaining position and recorded realized P&L of -$1.04. Its performance record at 20:36:32 UTC reports P&L of -$2.73 and return of -0.136605%; that P&L differs from the book’s realized P&L and cutoff equity fields, and the supplied records do not reconcile the measures.

The book proposed selling 0.097068 AMD shares. Deterministic risk approved the proposal, and the simulator recorded a fill at $503.25 at 20:36:32 UTC. This was a simulated fill, not a broker fill; no broker fill is recorded. The strongest recorded counterargument was that the position was small and a broad market decline might be temporary, allowing for a rebound. The decision’s recorded reasoning was that AMD had fallen below Friday’s low and its completed-session 20-day average during the planned review window.

The run summary also marks the SPY buy-and-hold comparison as FAILED because its quote postdated the valuation cutoff. That is a failed comparison calculation, not a trade fill or deliberate wait.

Every holding

MU — mean-reversion

The book holds 0.053191 MU shares at an average purchase price of $939.88. Its recorded value is $38.37 and its supplied unrealized loss is $11.63, excluding fees. The supplied current_price is null, but an observed_price is available: $721.31 at 2026-11-16 21:00 UTC. That is an observed bid/ask midpoint, not a live price; the reported bid was $683.29 and ask $759.33, whose midpoint is $721.31.

Today’s book review says MU’s original investment thesis, expected review window, and invalidation conditions are unavailable, so the original case cannot be fully checked. It notes that current financial results are available, including a 9.67 trailing earnings multiple and 7.25% reported cash-flow yield, but the 74.59% operating margin is a retained historical maximum. The recorded price trend was weak, and no trade was proposed. The strongest counterargument is that the low earnings multiple and strong reported results could reflect attractive value; the recorded concern is that peak profitability and weak price action do not establish a current turnaround. The available records do not supply the original thesis.

Read prices with their timestamps

Snapshots have timestamps. The MU midpoint observation at 21:00 UTC came before the report cutoff at 22:00 UTC, and book performance records can be earlier still. A recorded value describes the observation used at that time; it does not guarantee a closing or live quote.

A worked example of a midpoint mark

For MU, the supplied bid was $683.29 and ask was $759.33. Their midpoint is ($683.29 + $759.33) ÷ 2 = $721.31. The holding’s reported value uses that midpoint; the wide bid/ask range is a reminder that the midpoint is a valuation mark, not a promise of an executable price.

What to watch next

The paper and mean-reversion decisions list 2026-11-17 20:15 UTC for reconsideration. The AMD rationale says to review any remaining shares on November 17; the short-horizon book’s final position count is zero. The next report can check new decisions, fills, and snapshots without assuming any outcome in advance.

Deterministic risk: A rule-based check that records whether a proposed trade is approved or rejected.

Simulated fill: A recorded simulated transaction in a paper book; it does not establish a broker execution.

Bid/ask midpoint: The average of the recorded bid and ask, used here to value the MU holding.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
